newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: STAKE BUY NEWS FUELS JCI, LONRHO.
newsitem.headline: STAKE BUY NEWS FUELS JCI, LONRHO.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd's earlier announcement that it would acquire a substantial stake in British conglomerate Lonrho Plc launched the companies' shares higher on Thursday in active early trade, dealers said.
Within the first 30 minutes of trade Lonrho's South African listing jumped more than five percent, or 50 cents, to 10.40 rand with 205,200 shares changing hands.
JCI climbed nearly three percent, or 95 cents, to 34.20 rand in volume of 58,800 shares.

Just days after JCI and Lonrho's month-long merger talks collapsed last Monday, the South African group announced late Wednesday that it would acquire a 26.8 percent of Lonrho Plc for approximately 2.5 billion rand.
"The market has reacted very positively. It's seen as a step in the right direction," said James Scott at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Shortly after the announcment both JCI and Lonrho shares enjoyed much buying from the United States, he said.
"After the announcement there was much demand straight out of the States," Scott told Reuters.

JCI said that in terms of an agreement reached earlier, it had been granted call options on Anglo American Corp of South Africa , De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and The Southern Life Association's combined holdings of some 211.08 million Lonrho shares -- effectively a 26.8 percent stake.
In turn, JCI Ltd had granted the three companies put options on their stake in Lonrho. It said it would pay 11.64 rand or 155 pence per share for the stake.
"The options, exerciseable during December 1997, are conditional inter alia upon the approvals of the European Commission and the shareholders of JCI Ltd," it said.
But dealers noted that while the deal was seen as positive, it had yet to be finalised.
"It's nice to have the uncertainty removed, slightly, but you've got to keep in mind that it's not a done deal yet and there are so many other complexities, like Anglo and Ashanti," one dealer said.
The European Comission ruled in April that Anglo had to reduce its 27.5 percent stake in Lonrho to 9.99 percent within two years to avoid controlling the platinum market.
Lonrho's prime international asset is its 33.6 percent stake in Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd which Anglo has made no secret of coveting.
Anglo said last week that Lonrho had suggested swapping its stake in Ashanti for Anglo's shares in Lonrho.
Dealers were of the opinion that any development involving Anglo would likely be seen as positive.
"And, if Anglo organises this Ashanti business, that will be taken as positive too," another dealer said.
Anglo's shares were last steady at 271 rand with 23,000 shares traded.
